critical.name: Classified-history-file test cannot fail and checks only one side
critical.summary:
test_a_classified_history_file_is_skipped_on_both_sides classifies docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json but never creates that file. In sweep_problems (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:333-334) a classified path absent on the side checked is dropped by absent_paths, so the test passes with or without the `not p.startswith(prefixes)` filter on line 327: removing the history skip of classified files leaves this test green. The name also says 'on both sides' but the test calls sweep_problems only without a rev (tree side); the base side is never asserted. The classified-side history skip is therefore uncovered (the driver test at tests/scripts/test_plan_driver.py:272 classifies no history file either).

Also (adv_code): The test classifies docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json but never creates that file, so the new absent_paths drop removes it from `unhit` whatever the classified-side history filter does. The test also checks only the tree side despite its name. The classified-side filter `not p.startswith(prefixes)` at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:327 is therefore untested: removing it keeps the suite green.

Also (tests): test_history_folders_are_not_sweep_hits writes docs/_commit_messages/x.txt without adding or committing it, so at `git rev-parse HEAD` (line 267) only docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json exists; the second assertion never exercises the _commit_messages prefix at a revision.

Attack: Change plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:327 to `classified = {p for p in sweep.hits if p != source}` (drop the history-prefix filter) and run `python -m pytest tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py -q -k classified_history_file`: it still passes, because docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json does not exist in the project, so absent_paths at plan_checks.py:334 removes it from the 'classified but has no hit' set. With the file created (any content), the same mutation makes the test fail with 'sweep S1: docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json is classified but has no hit'.
fix: Create the review in the project so it exists on both sides: `root = make_project(files={**FILES, "docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json": '{"pattern": "OLD_NAME"}\n'})`, then assert both `pc.sweep_problems(sweep_plan(hits), root, HISTORY) == []` and `pc.sweep_problems(sweep_plan(hits), root, HISTORY, git(root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")) == []`. With the file present and its hits skipped, dropping the classified-side filter yields 'is classified but has no hit', so the test can fail.

Create the review file in the test: root = make_project(files={**FILES, 'docs/PR_REVIEWS/LOCAL_x.json': '{"pattern": "OLD_NAME"}\n'}), and add the base-side assertion pc.sweep_problems(sweep_plan(hits), root, HISTORY, git(root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')) == [].

Pass the commit message through make_project's files dict (`{**FILES, review: ..., "docs/_commit_messages/x.txt": "rename OLD_NAME\n"}`) so it is committed, keeping the untracked-file case covered elsewhere, or `git add` and commit it before line 267.

important.name: Classified sweep path that exists on neither side is never reported
important.summary:
sweep_problems now drops every unhit classified path that absent_paths reports missing on the side checked (plan_checks.py:333-334). The tree check (rev None) and the base check (rev=base) each suppress a path missing on their own side, so a classification naming a path that exists nowhere (a typo such as src/old_nmae.py, or a file renamed before the base) passes both claim_problems and base_claim_problems (plan.py:342,444). In claims_rev mode only the base check runs, so the same holds there. Before this change such a path failed with 'is classified but has no hit'; the write-plan contract 'stale classifications fail' now holds only for files that exist. No test in tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py covers a classified path absent on both sides, so the gap is unguarded.

Also (roast): sweep_problems now drops every unhit classified path that absent_paths reports missing on the side checked (plan_checks.py:333-334). The excuse is meant for a file deleted after the base or added after it, but nothing requires the path to exist on the other side. A misspelled classification (`src/legasy.py`) or a stale entry for a file gone before the base is absent in the tree and at the base, so `check` (tree), the freeze's base pass (plan.py:443-444) and the mid-plan base-only check (claims_rev) all excuse it. Before this PR that case read `is classified but has no hit`; now it passes silently, and no test pins it (test_a_classified_file_present_at_the_base_without_hits_is_a_problem covers only a file that exists). The fix swapped a false positive for a false negative.

Also (adv_code): sweep_problems drops every classified path absent on the side checked (absent_paths at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_checks.py:334). freeze runs the tree check (claim_problems) and the base check (base_claim_problems), and a mid-plan check runs only the base side, but nothing requires a dropped path to exist on the other side. A misspelled or stale key in sweep.hits (a file that exists nowhere) is therefore absent in the tree and absent at the base, gets dropped both times, and the plan freezes with a bogus classification. Before this change the same key was reported as 'classified but has no hit'. The intended case (deleted after the base, or added after it) only needs the path to exist on one of the two sides.

Attack: Repo with one committed file src/old_name.py containing 'OLD_NAME = 1'; base = HEAD. Plan with sweep {'id': 'S1', 'pattern': 'OLD_NAME', 'hits': {'src/old_name.py': 'rewrite', 'src/old_nmae.py': 'typo'}}. pc.sweep_problems(plan, root, ('docs/PLANS',)) returns [] and pc.sweep_problems(plan, root, ('docs/PLANS',), base) returns [] (probe run at the PR head); at the merge base both calls returned ['sweep S1: src/old_nmae.py is classified but has no hit']. Through the driver: in tests/scripts/test_plan_driver.py, filled(sweeps=[{'id': 'S1', 'pattern': 'def add', 'hits': {**ADD_HITS, 'src/nowhere.py': 'typo'}}]) then run('freeze', '1') exits 0.
fix: Suppress an absent path only when it exists on the other side: with rev given, keep the path in the report unless (root / p).exists(); with rev None, take the plan's base as an extra argument (plan.py has plan.base_commit) and keep the path unless absent_paths(root, {p}, base) is empty. Add a test where a classified path exists in neither the tree nor the base and expect 'is classified but has no hit' (or a distinct 'exists on neither side' line).
Keep the per-side suppression but have plan.py intersect the absent sets of the tree and base checks and report the paths absent on both as a separate problem.

Excuse an absent classified path only when it exists on the other side: give sweep_problems (or absent_paths) the counterpart (the base rev when checking the tree, the working tree when checking a rev) and keep `is classified but has no hit` for a path absent on both; add a test with a classification naming a file that exists nowhere.
Add a separate problem line, e.g. `sweep S1: <path> is classified but exists neither in the tree nor at the base`, computed in plan.py where both sides are known, and test it.

Drop an absent classified path only when it exists on the other side: give sweep_problems the plan's base_commit (or the other rev) and keep a path in `unhit` when it is absent both in the tree and at the base; report it as e.g. 'sweep S1:

exists neither in the tree nor at the base'.

Alternatively keep sweep_problems as is and add a separate check in plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py (claim_problems) that flags any sweep.hits key absent both in the working tree and at plan.base_commit (git cat-file --batch-check), and add a test in tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py with a key such as 'src/old_nmae.py' expecting a problem.

important.name: Driver test's 'deleted after the base' file never exists at the base
important.summary: test_a_sweep_hit_deleted_or_added_after_the_base_freezes commits src/legacy.py on feat-x (lines 257-259), then `new` (inside filled) records base_commit as the merge base with main (plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:277), which predates that commit. legacy.py is therefore absent at the base and absent in the tree, so its 'deleted on the branch' classification is dropped by absent_paths on both freeze (base side, plan.py:444) and check (tree side, plan.py:342) without ever having a hit. The deleted-after-base half of the scenario the name claims is not exercised at the driver level; only fresh.py does real work.
fix: Move main onto the legacy commit before the plan is created, e.g. add `git(project, "branch", "-f", "main", "HEAD")` after line 259, so the merge base holds legacy.py with its `def add` hit and the freeze-at-base sweep sees it.
Alternatively commit legacy.py on main (`git checkout -q main`, commit, `git checkout -q -B feat-x main`) before calling filled().
